title: An announcement in the square
summary: The harbor master's clerk reads a notice to the market square. Ines and Leo hear it. The town talks: by the next day (world_time +1) everyone in the harbor and town groups knows; Mira, alone at the light, only by the third day. Ines's private aside about who the clerk is spreads to nobody.

notice.label: the harbor master's notice
notice.truth: The harbor master is closing the north quay for the winter and every boat must move round to Skerry Cove.

wilf.label: how Ines knew early
wilf.truth: The harbor master's clerk is Ines's nephew Wilf, and he told her about the notice a week early.

spine.text: Noon in Saltmere's market square. Stalls, gulls, wet cobbles. Ines is buying onions; Leo is with her, carrying the basket.
Not those, love, they're soft. The ones at the back.

The harbor master's clerk climbs onto the trough by the pump, unrolls a notice, and bawls it out to the whole square: by order, the north quay closes for the winter, and every boat moves round to Skerry Cove by the first of the month.
Skerry Cove? Where's that?
Round the headland, an hour's row. The men will be furious.

spine.hint: Ines reacts to the notice and says who will take it worst.

spine.text: *Quieter.* My sister's boy Wilf is the clerk. He told me a week ago and I said nothing. You see? I can keep a secret.
I'm impressed.

spine.hint: Ines is pleased with herself and tells Leo how the square will take the news.

spine.text: The square fills with noise as the news goes from stall to stall.

spine.hint: Ines points out the fishermen's wives arguing by the pump.

spine.text: That evening the Bell is quiet. The harbor men haven't come in yet. Ines and Leo sit by the fire, sorting the onions.

spine.hint: Ines talks about how the town has changed since the Halcyon.

spine.text: Will Tom have to move the Petrel?
Everyone will, love. He doesn't know yet, I'd wager. He's been out at the crab since dawn.

spine.hint: Ines guesses how Tom and Rook will take the news when they hear it.

probe.ask: Tom, any news from the harbor master lately?
Rook, where will the boats winter this year?
Mira, has the harbor master said anything that touches the light?
Ines, where do the boats have to go this winter?

spine.text: Next morning on the quay. Tom and Rook stand looking at the empty north berths, where the harbor master's men have chalked numbers on the stones.
Chalk on the stones. They mean it, then.
Meant it from the start.

spine.hint: Tom and Rook talk about the move and how far it is to row there every morning.

spine.text: Who told you, anyway?
Whole town's saying it. Had it from the baker's lad before the sun was up.

spine.hint: Tom and Rook complain about the harbor master.

spine.text: Leo comes down the quay steps.
Here's the man. You were in the square yesterday, weren't you? Did you hear it read?
Every word. Ines bought onions through the whole thing.

spine.hint: Tom and Rook ask Leo what the square was like when the notice was read.

probe.ask: Tom, where are the boats going this winter?
Rook, where's the fleet off to?
Mira, has the harbor master's news reached you out at the light?
Tom, who's the clerk who read the notice?

spine.scene: The Drowned Bell, the taproom, that night

spine.text: That night the Bell is packed with angry fishermen. Ines can't pour fast enough. Tom, Rook and Leo hold the end of the bar.
If one more of you tells me it's my fault, you can row there yourselves tonight.

spine.hint: The three of them talk over the move and what it will cost the town.

spine.text: Who even writes these notices? Some clerk with ink on his nose.
*She becomes very busy with a glass.* Couldn't say, love.

spine.hint: Tom wonders who in the harbor office knew in advance; Ines changes the subject.

spine.text: Row an hour there, an hour back. Half the catch gone in the rowing.
Can't the town petition the harbor master?

spine.hint: Tom and Rook laugh at the idea of petitioning anyone in Saltmere.

spine.text: Afternoon. Tom rows out to the light with coal and finds Mira on the gallery, cleaning the glass.
You're early. And sour.

spine.hint: Tom grumbles to his sister about the harbor master's notice.

spine.text: Hm. They never ask the light about anything.

spine.hint: Mira and Tom talk about the coming winter.

spine.text: I'll be back Thursday with oil.

spine.scene: The market square, three days later

spine.text: Three days later, market day again. Mira has come in for lamp oil and finds Ines at the onion stall with Leo.
Everyone in this square looks like a wet cat. What's happened?
Oh, love, haven't you heard? Where have you been?
Up a lighthouse.

spine.hint: Ines tells Mira what's been going on in town this week.
Mira says what she thinks of it.

probe.ask: Mira, where will your brother keep his boat this winter?
Mira, who's the harbor master's clerk these days?
Ines, who's the clerk at the harbor office?

spine.text: I'll carry your oil, Mira.
You'll carry it to the causeway and no further.

spine.hint: Ines says goodbye and goes back to her stall.
Mira, walking off with Leo, says something dry about the town.
